title: A Font That Reads Fine to You and Gibberish to a Scraper
hook: ShieldFont scrambles the underlying characters of a web page while rendering the words normally — so humans read the article and AI crawlers harvest nonsense.
key_points: ShieldFont is a typeface designed to poison AI training data scraped from web pages.
The glyphs a reader sees don't match the character codes a crawler copies.
Pages stay readable for people; the scraped text comes out as garbage.
It's part of a wider shift from asking crawlers not to scrape to making scraping useless.
Trade-offs are real: text encoded this way resists copy-paste, search, and screen readers.
content_html: Website owners who don't want their words feeding AI models have mostly had two options: ask crawlers politely to stay away, or sue. ShieldFont, covered by Ars Technica, tries a third: make the harvest worthless. The typeface renders text that looks perfectly normal to a reader while the characters actually stored in the page are scrambled, so an automated crawler copying the text away ends up with gibberish.
extra_html:
This is data poisoning applied to typography, and it's a neat illustration of why the scraping fight is shifting. Signals like robots.txt only work if the crawler chooses to obey them; poisoning doesn't ask permission, it just lowers the value of what gets taken.

The catch is that scrapers aren't the only software that reads the real characters. Screen readers, browser search, copy-paste, translation tools, and search-engine indexing all depend on the text underneath matching the text on screen. Break that link and you break accessibility and discoverability along with the crawlers — which is why approaches like this tend to stay a targeted tactic rather than a default for the whole web.

related.title: Where AI Learns From
related.hook: An AI is a mirror of its training data — and most big models learned from a giant scrape of the public internet. That explains both their broad knowledge and their inherited flaws.

related.title: A Web Scraper Beat Google and Reddit in Court
related.hook: "Google and Reddit do not own the Internet," the winner said — after a court rejected their attempt to use copyright takedown law to stop a company from collecting public web pages.

related.title: A Hack Exposed What an AI Music Generator Trained On
related.hook: Suno never said what music trained its AI. A hacking incident did the talking instead, reportedly exposing millions of songs and lyrics scraped from YouTube, Genius, and Deezer.

flashcards.prompt: How does ShieldFont make a page unreadable to AI scrapers but fine for people?
flashcards.back_html: The characters stored in the page don't match the shapes the font draws. A reader sees normal words; a crawler copying the underlying text gets nonsense.

flashcards.prompt: What broader strategy does ShieldFont represent?

choices.text: Data poisoning — making scraped content worthless rather than merely asking crawlers to stay out
Suing every company that trains on web data
Encrypting websites so only paying readers can load them

flashcards.explanation_html: Politeness signals like robots.txt rely on crawlers cooperating. Poisoning changes the economics by degrading the value of whatever gets taken.

flashcards.prompt: What's a real cost of publishing text this way?

choices.text: Anything depending on the true characters — copy-paste, search, screen readers — breaks too
The page loads images at lower quality
Visitors have to install the font themselves

flashcards.explanation_html: A scraper and a screen reader both read the underlying characters. Scrambling them hurts assistive tech and search along with the crawlers.
